extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, IP professionals, and clients interested in EPO case law
extracted.subtask_description: Summarises recent EPO Boards of Appeal decisions and referrals on description amendments, videoconference oral proceedings, and prior-use enablement; intended to convey practical legal standards and unresolved questions for EPO practice. Useful for practitioners handling opposition/appeal strategy and claim/description drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments in opposition require a ground of opposition (Rule 80 EPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in Opposition should be occasioned by a ground of Opposition (Rule 80 EPC). A lack of clarity under Article 84 EPC is not a ground for Opposition, except in cases where the lack of clarity arises solely as a result of a post-grant amendment (G 3/14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adaptation of the description in opposition is not appropriate unless a new discrepancy between the description and the claims had arisen as a result of a post-grant amendment. T2391/18 confirms that a granted patent cannot be invalidated solely on the grounds that the claims are unclear because the description was not adequately adapted before grant (Article 84 EPC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amended claims introducing new limitations must be accompanied by adapted description
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amended claims submitted during opposition that include limitations not present in the granted claims should always be accompanied by a corresponding amended description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from T2391/18: when claim scope is narrowed or altered by post-grant claim amendments in opposition, the description should be adapted to remove or reconcile discrepancies between claims and description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of the patent application has no role in claim interpretation (use only granted patent description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the description of the granted patent may be used for claim interpretation under Article 69(1) EPC; the description of the patent application plays no role in claim interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies irrespective of whether the description was adapted prior to grant (T450/20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not 'mine' the description for limiting definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The description of a patent could not be mined for a definition limiting the meaning of the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: T450/20: courts/boards should not take isolated passages from the description to impose limiting definitions on claim terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional language in the description may be used to construe claims
rubrics_metrics.description: It is permissible to use functional language from the description to construe the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While mining for limiting definitions is disallowed, functional formulations in the description can legitimately inform claim construction (T450/20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of witness credibility in videoconference (ViCo) oral proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearing a witness in first instance proceedings by videoconference allowed sufficient interaction between the deciding body, the parties and the witness; partial lack of visible body language does not automatically infringe the parties' right to be heard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credibility should be judged mainly on the conclusiveness of the testimony and the absence of contradictions: within the witness' own testimony, between multiple witnesses' testimonies, and between testimony and information derivable from supporting documents (T423/22).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-use enablement question: scope of exclusion from prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Question whether the non-enabling prior use of a product excludes the composition of the product from the prior art or whether it also excludes the product per se (i.e., so that it cannot be used as a starting point for inventive step).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central issue in the G1/23 referral arising from T0438/19 and seeks clarification from the Enlarged Board of Appeal on how non-enabling prior use should affect what constitutes prior art for both composition and product analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-use enablement question: definition of 'enablement' for a prior-used product
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarification sought over the definition of 'enablement' with respect to the prior use of a product, particularly whether 'enablement' requires that the skilled person be able to fully analyse and reproduce the exact same product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: G1/23 referral asks whether enablement for prior use demands full analytical/reproducibility capability by the skilled person, which affects whether that prior use is treated as prior art for composition and inventive-step assessments.
